rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard Metropolis MC for the 2D HPZ model; requires implementing the Hamiltonian with random anisotropy, field cycling, and quench protocol. While not research-grade novel, it demands careful translation of physics into code and understanding of phase transitions.
rationale.execution: Multiple sequential simulation stages: generate disorder, run field-sweep hysteresis, loop over temperatures for coercive field, quench-warming protocol; each stage requires proper MC equilibration and measurement. Standard libraries only, but orchestration is nontrivial.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard Monte Carlo simulation of a well-known spin model; implementation requires nontrivial Metropolis algorithm and data collection but no novel methods. The pipeline involves multiple simulation runs and protocols, but complexity is moderate.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Simulates a 64x64 lattice with O(10^5-10^6) Monte Carlo steps per run; runs efficiently on a single CPU core with minimal memory and no external data.
